title: Rigidity at the Extremal Crouzeix Constant
content: For a complex matrix \(A\), let \(\psi(A)\) be the norm of the polynomial functional calculus on its numerical range. We prove that \(\psi(A)=2\) only when the numerical range is a nondegenerate closed disk. The proof first extracts the equality conditions in the sharp double-layer estimate. After boundary eigenvalues are removed, an extremizer obtained from a finite Blaschke product satisfies an exact boundary-kernel identity. On a curved exposed arc this identity makes the extremizer rational. A direct resolvent argument then places every zero of its reduced numerator inside the numerical range and every pole outside; consequently its full unit lemniscate coincides with the boundary of the numerical range. The defining polynomial of the projective dual of that algebraic boundary divides the Hermitian Kippenhahn determinant. Hyperbolicity and strict convexity force the dual curve to have degree two, and its points at infinity force the resulting conic to be a circle.
